todays_goal: Launch a new laptop-only TacticLab build after TransferLab completion.

lessons.subject: computer_science
lessons.unit_title: Creative Technology and AI Builder Lab
lessons.previous_learning: TransferLab Version 1 was completed on Day 17, including a real-player creative upgrade.
lessons.course_context: Begin a new laptop-only build emphasizing drag-and-drop UI, state, persistence, constraints, and UX.
lessons.why_it_matters: This develops practical interactive-product skill: event-driven UI, state, persistence, constraints, and UX.

vocabulary.definition: moving an interface object by dragging it
keeping saved state so it can be restored later
the planned arrangement of players on the pitch

lessons.written_instruction: Laptop only. Build TacticLab with three formations, draggable players, save, and reset using natural-language vibe coding.

worked_examples.title: State flow
worked_examples.solution: Load default positions -> render -> drag updates -> save.
worked_examples.explanation: The app remembers formation and locations.

guided_practice.prompt: Whiteboard the pitch, 4-3-3 positions, state flow, and acceptance criteria.

independent_practice.prompt: Test formation switching, dragging, save, and reset.
After core criteria pass, add one creative feature.

exit_ticket.prompt: Demo TacticLab and explain what state it remembers.
exit_ticket.answer: Formation and player locations, plus saved lineup state.

lessons.voice_prompt: Laptop only. Use the whiteboard for pitch layout, positions, state flow, and acceptance criteria. Do not teach syntax. Help Atticus write precise vibe-coding requests and test behavior.
